subject: Problems with group.equal constraints for growth curve models

messages.author: c1a4b8dfa3d622e1
messages.subject: Problems with group.equal constraints for growth curve models
parts:
I'm currently testing out a multiple groups latent-basis growth curve model starting with the invariance model first and relaxing the constraints. My model is specified as: 

lgcm.syntax <-'
intercept =~ 1*verb1 + 1*verb2 + 1*verb4 + 1*verb6
slope  =~ 0*verb1 +   verb2 +   verb4 + 5*verb6
# equal residual variance 
verb1 ~~ rv1*verb1
verb2 ~~ rv1*verb2
verb4 ~~ rv1*verb4
verb6 ~~ rv1*verb6
'

I then run the following: 

# Invariance 
invariant.mod <- growth(lgcm.syntax, data = wisc, missing = "fiml", fixed.x = F, group = "grad", group.equal = c("means", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances", "loadings", "residuals"))
summary(invariant.mod, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, rsquare = T)

# Means  
means.mod <- growth(lgcm.syntax, data = wisc, missing = "fiml", fixed.x = F, group = "grad", group.equal = c("lv.variances", "lv.covariances", "loadings", "residuals"))
summary(means.mod, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, rsquare = T)

# Variances/Covariances   
meansvar.mod <- growth(lgcm.syntax, data = wisc, missing = "fiml", fixed.x = F, group = "grad", group.equal = c("loadings", "residuals"))
summary(meansvar.mod, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, rsquare = T)

Everything is fine up until this point... 

# Curves  
curves.mod <- growth(lgcm.syntax, data = wisc, missing = "fiml", fixed.x = F, group = "grad", group.equal = c("residuals"))
summary(curves.mod, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, rsquare = T)

After running this model, taking away group.equal = "loadings", the residuals are estimated to be different across time for my 2nd group (there are only 2 groups), however, in my growth model, they're specified to be equal across time:

# Residuals
residuals.mod <- growth(lgcm.syntax, data = wisc, missing = "fiml", fixed.x = F, group = "grad")
summary(residuals.mod, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, rsquare = T)

The same happens here as well. 

Any clue on what might be going on?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Problems with group.equal constraints for growth curve models
parts:
On 02/19/2014 01:27 AM, Randy B wrote:

> verb1 ~~ rv1*verb1
> verb2 ~~ rv1*verb2
> verb4 ~~ rv1*verb4
> verb6 ~~ rv1*verb6

This is dangerous syntax is a multiple group analysis (and perhaps I
should make it illegal, throwing an error).

Currently (0.5-15), this syntax will fix the (residual) variances to be
equal in the first group only. If you want them to be equal in the other
groups, you need to write something like (assuming 3 groups):

verb1 ~~ c(rv1, rv2, rv3)*verb1
verb2 ~~ c(rv1, rv2, rv3)*verb2
verb4 ~~ c(rv1, rv2, rv3)*verb4
verb6 ~~ c(rv1, rv2, rv3)*verb6

I would suggest NOT to use the group.equal="residuals" option in this
setting. If you need them to be equal both within and across groups,
just write

verb1 ~~ c(rv1, rv1, rv1)*verb1
verb2 ~~ c(rv1, rv1, rv1)*verb2
verb4 ~~ c(rv1, rv1, rv1)*verb4
verb6 ~~ c(rv1, rv1, rv1)*verb6

and all will be fine.

Yves.
